speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please tell me about the onset and location of your abdominal pain, and whether you have noticed any changes in your bowel habits or stool color. Additionally, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or night sweats alongside your fatigue and fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given your history of type 2 diabetes and the darkening of your urine, we need to rule out a urinary tract issue or liver involvement. Can you tell me if you have noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or if you are passing clay-colored stools? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Urinalysis, CBC.

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis (likely Hepatitis A given the fair exposure).

The significantly elevated ALT and AST, coupled with the history of eating at a state fair and the clinical signs of liver dysfunction (jaundice, tender hepatomegaly), strongly point to acute viral hepatitis. I am requesting images of the liver and ultrasound to assess for any structural complications or ruling out other causes. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound
